previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, and polysubstance use was admitted for acute shortness of breath after missing medications and using crack cocaine. He presented with tachypnea, hypoxia, and signs of fluid overload. Imaging showed worsening bilateral lung opacities, and he was treated for both possible pneumonia and chemical pneumonitis from crack inhalation. He received a course of antibiotics and a short steroid regimen for lung inflammation, with gradual improvement in oxygenation. Acute kidney injury developed due to over-diuresis but resolved with fluid management. His diuretic was adjusted to 30mg torsemide, metoprolol was held due to cocaine use, and he was discharged home on a prednisone taper with follow-up plans. Social work addressed his housing instability and substance use.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Bronchitis and pneumonitis due to fumes and vapors
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ M with h/o CHF, COPD, crack cocaine use who 
presented with 1 week of worsening shortness of breath and new

# Shortess of breath:
Pt presented with 1 week of worsening dyspnea on exertion, PND 
and orthopnea. Etiology likely CHF exacerbation in addition to 
underlying pulmonary process (diffuse ground-glass opacities, 
bulky lymphadenopathy and spiculated lung mass on CTA concerning 
for possible lung CA). BNP found to be ~___, which is elevated 
but below his previous value of 5197 on ___. For CHF 
exacerbation, pt was started on IV Furosemide and eventually 
transitioned to Torsemide PO 30mg on HD2 once his SOB had 
improved. He put out ___ throughout his stay and crackles 
and edema concurrently improved. ECHO on HD2 showed worsening LV 
function from previous so on HD3 he was switched to 40mg 
Torsemide at the request of Dr. ___ cardiologist. In 
terms of the concerning findings on CTA, pulmonology was 
consulted and eventually recommended that IP biopsy the nodule.  
They were unable to biopsy the lung nodule because the patient 
became hemodynamically unstable with anesthesia with BP to 
___.  They were able to biopsy an enlarged lymph node.  He 
will follow up with Dr. ___ can decide how to procede in 
terms of the right upper lobe nodule.  He was continued on his 
home COPD regimen (albuterol, fluticasone-salmeterol, 
tiotropium) initially, but this was discontinued because he does 
not have COPD, but rather has a restrictive pattern on PFTs.

depressions on EKG concerning for unstable angina vs. NSTEMI.

nitroglycerine, aspirin and Metoprolol in the ED. Chest pain

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with a history of COPD, CHF, and crack/cocaine use,
now with one-week history of shortness of breath and one-day history of chest
pain.

STUDY:  Chest CTA; MDCT images were generated through the chest after the
uneventful IV administration of 100 cc of Omnipaque intravenous contrast in
the pulmonary arterial phase.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were
generated as well as right and left oblique maximum intensity projection
images.

COMPARISON:  ___.  ___ chest CTA.

FINDINGS:  The aorta is normal in caliber without dissection.  The pulmonary
arterial trunk is at the upper limits of normal in size but shows no filling
defects to the subsegmental level.  The heart size is large with calcified
atherosclerotic disease present in the left coronary arterial branches.  Trace
pericardial effusion is present.

The lungs demonstrate moderate emphysema.  Large regions of ground glass
opacity and anatomic distortion in both lungs, remain from more severe
infiltration in those areas on the prior exam.  There are no new areas of
opacity.  A 13-mm spiculated nodule in the right upper lobe persists (2:31),
grown slightly since chest CT on ___.  

Severe, extensive mediastinal lymphadenopathy is longstanding and stable,
measuring up to 14 mm in the prevascular station (2:31), 2.7 cm in the
subcarinal, and 17 mm in the paratracheal (2:46 and 3:64 respectively), and
2.2 cm in the aortopulmonary window (3:70). Adenopathy of this size and
peristence can be seen with the chronic foreign body stimulation from illicit
drug use or may be due to HIV or other infection. Small bilateral pleural
effusions, right greater than left are non-hemorrhagic and have improved from
prior exam.

The visualized portion of the upper abdomen shows no abnormality.  The
visualized bones show no aggressive-appearing lytic or sclerotic lesion.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No PE or aortic dissection.
2.  Severee mphysema. 
3.  Improved diffuse lung abnormality is probably the chronic
residual--scarring, organized pneumonia, and hemorrhage--due to episodes of
acute reactions to illicit drug use.
3.  Cardiomegaly. Atherosclerotic calcification, left coronary arterial
branches.
4.  13-mm spiculated nodule in the right upper lobe, which is similar to prior
exam, but has grown a little since ___, suspicious for lung
cancer.
5.  Stable, severe, chronic mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

HISTORY:  History of CHF, COPD and crack cocaine use who presents with 1 week
of shortness of breath.  Question change from previous.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

In comparison to previous radiograph, diffuse lung opacities have somewhat
decreased with some residual opacities predominently in the lower lobes.  No
pleural effusion or pneumothorax is present.  Right upper lobe linear opacity
is unchanged from prior.  Stable mild cardiomegaly.  

IMPRESSION:

Interval improvement in diffuse bilateral opacities.  No new consolidation.
